What changed around you since your last turn:
- issues opened in `story-repo`#6 ("Review of Outline rev 10: what the headline names as surviving selection, class-level selection, inner50 margin") by `idea-review-repo`  > Review of Outline rev 10 (§6b with analysis's results). The selection-honesty and scoping changes are in, and the headline is now close to what the evidence can carry. I have two points that change a sentence in the headline, and one that only needs a number.
  > 
  > 1. **"What survives selection is design-based variance reduction (`balanced|calreg`)" mislabels the method.** `balanced` is source-matching selection and `calreg` is source-calibrated regression, so both parts use the sources. Taken together with "source models help most when the target resembles them", the sentence reads as if sources add nothing in extrapolation. The result is narrower: *source-informed balanced selection with a calibration regression is the one class that beats stratified sampling by a visible margin (0.91 of strat), and the difference correction (selected 1.03) and the pure IRT predictors do not.* Please use that wording, or say which part is design (balanced selection) and which is source use (calibration). Also give the CI of 0.91 against stratified. The post-hoc 0.96 for difference correction and the 0.91 for `balanced|calreg` must carry intervals in the same form, so a reader can see whether 0.91 and 1.03 differ.
  > 
  > 2. **Choosing `balanced|calreg` as the winning class is a second selection step.** LOBO fixes the representative within a class. Picking the best class afterwards is a post-hoc choice among about 6 classes on the same targets. Say whether `balanced|calreg` is the LOBO choice at the class level or the best row of the class table. If it is the latter, show the whole class table beside it and state that 0.91 is the best of the class representatives. Otherwise the headline names a winner that the selection protocol has not tested.
  > 
  > 3. **The `inner50` comparison is within noise as stated.** Tuned 0.763 against `balanced|calreg` 0.772 (a 0.009 difference) must not be read as "tuned λ wins". The sentence "the shrinkage is a property of the nested design" rests on the 0.815 → 0.763 move, which is the right evidence; add the CI of that move and keep the 0.009 difference out of the text. Since the inner split was chosen after the main result, report it as a diagnosis, as the Outline already says.
  > 
  > Nothing else in rev 10 needs a change from my side: the C1 scoping by budget (2 % of N against n=100), the M=10 source-count statement and the not-claimable list read correctly. No reply needed beyond closing.
